### Data Cleaning
To be able to analyze the data from the different elections and compare the outcomes. Each dataset has to be cleaned. For some cantons e.g. Valais and Schwyz the data is very scattered, therefore for these multiple datasets per election have to be cleaned and merged.

The procedure for the data cleaning was the following: For each canton in alphabetically order, for each election the data was cleaned.

To ensure the compatibility of the different datasets, the column names were standardized. The column names were renamed for each dataset to the following: "total_votes", "svp_votes", "sp_votes", "cvp_votes", "fdp_votes", "glp_votes", "bdp_votes", "green_votes", "other_votes". It might be that some of the datasets do not contain all of these columns, since the party landscapes varies geographically and over time. 

```{r}
#| label: inspect-ag-09-raw

# Import and inspect the raw Aargau 2009 dataset
ag_09_raw <- read_excel(
  here("data", "datasets", "aargau", "AG_09_kantonsratswahlen.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Data"
)

glimpse(ag_09_raw)
print(ag_09_raw, n = 20)
names(ag_09_raw)
```

```{r}

# The district seat magnitudes and the official 2009 party seat totals
# are taken from the official Aargau election documentation and are
# hard-coded here as fixed inputs for the counterfactual exercise.

# THEREFORE LOOK IF POSSIBLE TO FIND DATASET WITH THE SEAT MAGNITUDES AND THE OFFICIAL 2009 PARTY SEAT TOTALS
ag_09_district_seats <- c(
  "Bezirk Aarau" = 16L,
  "Bezirk Baden" = 30L,
  "Bezirk Bremgarten" = 16L,
  "Bezirk Brugg" = 11L,
  "Bezirk Kulm" = 9L,
  "Bezirk Laufenburg" = 7L,
  "Bezirk Lenzburg" = 12L,
  "Bezirk Muri" = 7L,
  "Bezirk Rheinfelden" = 10L,
  "Bezirk Zofingen" = 15L,
  "Bezirk Zurzach" = 7L
)

ag_09_parties <- c(
  "svp", "sp", "cvp", "fdp", "gruene", "evp", "sd",
  "edu", "bdp", "uns", "glp", "npak", "l_plus", "faag"
)

# Keep the district results and convert "..." (party did not stand) to zero
ag_09_districts <- ag_09_raw |>
  clean_names() |>
  filter(location_type == "DISTRICT") |>
  mutate(
    district_seats = unname(ag_09_district_seats[location_name]),
    across(
      c(total, all_of(ag_09_parties)),
      ~ replace_na(as.numeric(na_if(as.character(.x), "...")), 0)
    )
  )

# Aargau's 2005 Hagenbach-Bischoff allocation, applied separately
# within each district. The main counterfactual assumes no list alliances.
allocate_hb <- function(votes, n_seats) {
  distribution_number <- floor(sum(votes) / (n_seats + 1)) + 1
  seats <- floor(votes / distribution_number)

  while (sum(seats) < n_seats) {
    quotients <- votes / (seats + 1)
    winner <- which.max(quotients)
    seats[winner] <- seats[winner] + 1L
  }

  as.integer(seats)
}

ag_09_hb_by_district <- ag_09_districts |>
  select(location_name, district_seats, all_of(ag_09_parties)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(ag_09_parties),
    names_to = "parties",
    values_to = "party_votes"
  ) |>
  group_by(location_name) |>
  mutate(
    seats_hb = allocate_hb(party_votes, first(district_seats)),
    voter_number = floor(
      party_votes / first(district_seats) + 0.5
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Official party seat totals under Double Pukelsheim in 2009
ag_09_dp_seats <- tribble(
  ~parties, ~seats_dp,
  "SVP",          45L,
  "SP",           22L,
  "CVP",          21L,
  "FDP",          20L,
  "GRUENE",       13L,
  "EVP",           6L,
  "SD",            2L,
  "EDU",           2L,
  "BDP",           4L,
  "UNS",           0L,
  "GLP",           5L,
  "NPAK",          0L,
  "L_PLUS",        0L,
  "FAAG",          0L
)

# Final election-party dataset
ag_09_clean <- ag_09_hb_by_district |>
  group_by(parties) |>
  summarise(
    voter_number = sum(voter_number),
    seats_hb = sum(seats_hb),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    parties = str_to_upper(parties),
    vote_share = 100 * voter_number / sum(voter_number),
    small_party = as.integer(vote_share < 10)
  ) |>
  left_join(ag_09_dp_seats, by = "parties") |>
  transmute(
    election_id = "AG_09",
    parties,
    vote_share = round(vote_share, 4),
    small_party,
    seats_hb = as.integer(seats_hb),
    seats_dp = as.integer(seats_dp)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(vote_share))

# Validation and inspection
stopifnot(
  identical(
    names(ag_09_clean),
    c("election_id", "parties", "vote_share", "small_party",
      "seats_hb", "seats_dp")
  ),
  nrow(ag_09_clean) == length(ag_09_parties),
  sum(ag_09_clean$seats_hb) == 140L,
  sum(ag_09_clean$seats_dp) == 140L,
  abs(sum(ag_09_clean$vote_share) - 100) < 0.01
)

glimpse(ag_09_clean)
print(ag_09_clean, n = Inf)
```

For the counterfactual, the 2009 district-level party votes and the 2009 district seat magnitudes are retained. The Hagenbach--Bischoff allocation follows Sections 12--13 of the Aargau Grossratswahlgesetz used for the 2005 election: the distribution number is the next integer above the valid party votes divided by the number of seats plus one; initial seats are the integer quotients; and remaining seats are assigned sequentially using the largest quotient of party votes divided by seats already received plus one (Kanton Aargau, 2004, pp. 6--7). Although Section 8 allowed list alliances in 2005, the main counterfactual treats every party independently because list alliances were abolished for the 2009 Double Pukelsheim election. The district seat magnitudes are the official assignments for the 2009 election (Staatskanzlei des Kantons Aargau, 2008), while `seats_dp` records the officially reported result (Statistisches Amt des Kantons Aargau, 2009). Vote shares use the cantonal *Wählerzahl*: each district's party votes are divided by its seat magnitude and rounded to the nearest integer before cantonal aggregation (Grossratswahlgesetz, Section 14).
